runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner with Dan Skelton's excellent 11/30 record, 21 days since last run optimal, prominent style suits likely pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Ballykinlar
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from Mickey Bowen yard, 44-day break potentially freshening, headgear change suggests connections seeking improvement.

runners_data.name: King Ulanda
runners_data.note: Recent winner carrying 6lb penalty, top-hat headgear indicates breathing issues, Greenall/Guerriero pair improving.

runners_data.name: Tom Doniphon
runners_data.note: Long 208-day absence major concern despite previous winning form, Hobbs/White combination below par this season.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: Inconsistent recent form from same stable as favourite, falls in last run worrying, needs to prove reliability.

races.paceDynamic: Tellherthename will likely take up the early running with all five runners showing prominent tendencies, but no confirmed pacesetter creates a moderate gallop scenario. The lack of a natural front-runner means the pace will be steady rather than strong, with Tellherthename, Ballykinlar and King Ulanda likely to dispute the early lead. This sustainable pace will not stretch the field early, allowing the entire field to remain competitive deep into the race. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and those with a strong finishing kick, as the modest gallop will set up a sprint finish where class and acceleration matter most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Tellherthename dictates a steady rhythm from the front without serious early pressure.
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows all runners to travel comfortably before a tactical finish where OR ratings become decisive. Tellherthename's class advantage (OR 132) and Dan Skelton's excellent form become crucial factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of natural pace-setters creates a crawling gallop through the early stages.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where Tom Doniphon's two-win form from last season and King Ulanda's recent victory become significant assets. Fresh legs and tactical speed prove more valuable than sustained galloping.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Multi-Horse Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Ballykinlar and King Ulanda force genuine early fractions alongside Tellherthename.
scenarios.body: The stronger gallop exposes stamina limitations and favours horses with proven staying power at this trip. Ice In The Veins' inconsistency becomes costly while the proven stayers benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If all five runners refuse to commit early, creating an unsustainable crawl.
scenarios.body: The race turns into a pure class-based sprint where ratings and recent form become irrelevant compared to tactical position and acceleration. Any horse can win from any position in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Tom Doniphon's market movement given 208-day layoff - connections may know something about readiness
King Ulanda's jumping under pressure carrying penalty weight after recent victory
Tellherthename's early position - if taken on for lead, pace dynamics change completely
Ice In The Veins' behaviour at start given recent fall and inconsistent jumping record
Ballykinlar's response to headgear change and whether it solves previous finishing problems

races.paceDynamic: L'Amalric will lead from the start with no genuine pace pressure in this small field, setting a comfortable rhythm over the first mile. Eternal Angel and Ladies Day will track closely in second and third, while the hold-up horses Pretty Darn Quick and Knolton Park will settle towards the rear with plenty to find. The lack of early pace will create a sprint finish from the last hurdle, with L'Amalric having first run but vulnerable to closers if the pace becomes too sedate. This tactical setup strongly favours prominent runners who can position close to the pace and have the speed to respond when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Comfortable Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If L'Amalric maintains a steady but honest gallop throughout without going too slow
scenarios.body: The leader gets an easy time of it and has enough left to repel late challenges, with prominent trackers best placed to pick up the pieces. Hold-up horses find themselves with too much ground to make up in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sedate Early Becomes Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If L'Amalric goes too slow early and the pace collapses into a crawl
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test from the last hurdle with horses coming from all angles in a cavalry charge finish. Those with the best turn of foot from prominent positions will prevail over the genuinely slow starters.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Crumbles Late
scenarios.trigger: If L'Amalric hits the front too soon and empties out before the line
scenarios.body: The prominent trackers inherit the lead but face pressure from improving hold-up horses who finally get into contention. This creates a genuine battle between mid-race positioning and finishing kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scoro Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the lightly-raced Scoro shows significant improvement and gets into the mix
scenarios.body: Brian Hughes produces the enigma from an impossible position to create chaos in the finish. The form horses would need to underperform significantly for this longshot scenario.

watchPoints.text: Pretty Darn Quick has been fading in recent finishes and the predicted lack of pace will make life even harder for this hold-up performer
L'Amalric could go too slow early as the unopposed leader and become vulnerable to anything with a finishing kick
Scoro represents the complete unknown factor after such a long absence and could either run a big race or disappoint completely
The small field size means any mistakes at hurdles will be costly as there's little room for recovery
Eternal Angel and Ladies Day will likely track the leader together and their battle could decide the winner

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front runner in this 14-runner field, the early pace will be tentative as the hold-up brigade waits for someone else to do the donkeywork. This creates a steadily-run affair that builds into a sprint finish over the final 3-4 furlongs at Uttoxeter. The lack of natural pace-setters means the field will bunch up turning for home, creating a cavalry charge finish where positioning and a turn of foot matter more than stamina. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can quicken off a modest gallop, disadvantaging those who need a truly-run race to show their best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays modest throughout and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows tactical operators with a turn of foot to position perfectly and strike late. Horses needing a strong gallop are found wanting when the tempo finally lifts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Injection
scenarios.trigger: If one of the better horses forces the issue from the 6f pole
scenarios.body: A mid-race move creates just enough tempo to string out the field without becoming truly strongly-run. This suits horses who can travel and have both stamina and speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Genuine Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Onehundredneighty or Saint Vic take them along from the start
scenarios.body: A genuinely-run race from flag to finish creates a proper test where stamina matters more than a turn of foot. The 2m4f trip becomes a true staying test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Bunch Sprint Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field is still tightly bunched at the last hurdle
scenarios.body: A messy finish where luck in running and avoiding trouble matters more than ability. Form horses get hampered while outsiders sneak through on the rails.

watchPoints.text: Sims' Law and Celine Man have both shown recent tendencies to fade or pull up and could impact the race if stopping suddenly

races.paceDynamic: Let's Sail Away will lead from the front with minimal pressure, establishing a controlled gallop over this extended 3-mile trip. With 8 of 10 runners preferring hold-up tactics, there's insufficient pace pressure to create a testing gallop early. The lack of prominent runners means Let's Sail Away can dictate terms throughout, likely quickening from 3 out when the field begins to close. This moderate tempo strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can track the pace, while hold-up horses face a scramble from the back when the race ignites late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Sail Away gets an easy lead without early challenges
scenarios.body: The pace stays sedate until the home turn, allowing the leader to kick clear when others are still organizing their challenges. Front-runners and prominent racers get first run on tired legs while hold-up horses struggle to make up ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Stampede Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up brigade closes dramatically from 2 out
scenarios.body: The slow early pace leaves plenty in reserve for a cavalry charge, creating a bunched finish where class and finishing kick matter most. Superior animals like Jo Arengeot Bey and Lynsey Larue can unleash devastating late runs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midrace Pace Injection
scenarios.trigger: If Twp Stori or another challenger moves up to pressure Let's Sail Away from 4 out
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates a more honest gallop, suiting horses with stamina reserves. Those who can track the increased pace without overracing gain crucial positioning advantages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Collapse Behind
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Sail Away builds an unassailable lead through lack of pace pressure
scenarios.body: The leader gets so far clear that even a late rally cannot bridge the gap, creating a procession. Only those tracking the winner or racing prominently have any realistic winning chance.

The lack of pace pressure means Order Of The Dance can dictate terms throughout the first circuit before the real race begins approaching the final fences. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can position handy and kick when the pace lifts, rather than hold-up horses who may find insufficient pace to close into.

scenarios.trigger: If Mistral Blue gets soft sectionals and isn't headed turning in
